title: Night Sky Quiz
intro: A few questions about what is up there. No pressure, and no one is keeping score but you.

questions.prompt: Which star is closest to Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star, about 150 million kilometres away. The next nearest star system is more than 4 light-years away.

questions.prompt: Roughly how long does the Moon take to go through all its phases, from one full Moon to the next?
questions.explanation: The cycle of phases takes about 29.5 days, which is where the idea of a month comes from.

questions.prompt: Why does the Moon seem to change shape over a month?
choices: Earth's shadow covers different parts of it
We see more or less of its sunlit half as it orbits Earth
questions.explanation: Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun. As the Moon orbits Earth, we see more or less of that lit half, which makes the phases.

questions.prompt: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks reddish because its dust and rocks contain a lot of iron oxide, which is the same stuff as rust.

questions.prompt: Which planet is best known for its bright, wide rings?
questions.explanation: Saturn's rings are made of countless pieces of ice and rock. Other giant planets have rings too, but they are much fainter.

choices: A cloud high in our atmosphere
A galaxy that contains our Sun
A comet that returns every year
questions.explanation: The Milky Way is our home galaxy, a huge spinning collection of stars. From a dark place you can see a pale band of its stars across the sky.

questions.prompt: Why does the North Star seem to stay almost still while the other stars wheel around it?
choices: It is the closest star to Earth
It sits almost straight above Earth's north pole
It is the brightest star in the sky
It does not move at all
questions.explanation: Earth spins around an axis that points almost exactly at Polaris, so it hardly moves while the sky turns. It is not especially bright or near.

questions.prompt: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.explanation: Light travels extremely fast, but the Sun is far away, so it takes a little over 8 minutes. We always see the Sun as it was a few minutes ago.

choices: A star falling out of the sky
A tiny bit of rock or dust glowing as it burns up in the air
questions.explanation: It is called a meteor. A speck of space dust or rock hits the upper atmosphere at high speed and glows for a moment.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun and has the shortest year of any planet, at about 88 Earth days.

questions.prompt: What mostly causes the ocean tides?
choices: The pull of the Moon and the Sun
questions.explanation: The Moon's gravity pulls on the oceans most, with a smaller pull from the Sun. As Earth turns, the water rises and falls along the coasts.
